title: Audit-append **concurrency contention.** `SqlAuditSink` takes no application-level lock: two genuinely concurrent state-changing requests both read the same chain tip (`TipHashAsync`) and race the `audit.AuditEvents` `PreviousHash` UNIQUE index — the loser gets SQL error 2601 (duplicate key) and the whole operation **500s** (fail-closed, but a hard error rather than a retry). Accepted at design time (ADR-0009/0026 + the `SqlAuditSink.cs` `ponytail:` note — "negligible at ≤20-user on-prem scale; if it ever bites, serialize via `sp_getapplock` or retry"). **Reproduced 2026-07-13** by the P15b live VR: the SPA's login-time `Membership.ProfileSynced` append raced an immediate seed burst, so one `Research.MissionProposed` lost the race and 500'd (audit seq 12/13 both chained off tip `1f738021`). Fix (the pre-named upgrade path): a **bounded retry** on 2601/2627 inside `AppendAsync` — re-read tip, recompute hash, re-insert — which preserves chain linearity + the fail-closed guarantee; or `sp_getapplock` serialization. **2026-07-13 — operator chose to fix now**, then (after adversarial review) to fix it **robustly** rather than cheaply. Arc: a first pass added a bounded optimistic-retry in `SqlAuditSink`; CI then showed the 8-way stress case **deadlocks (SQL 1205)**, whose victim's transaction is rolled back → in-place retry cannot recover. A devil's-advocate review further found a **sink-level app lock is lock-order-unsafe** (handlers like `IssueDecision`/`VerifyAction` emit-then-write-more, inverting `{lock, module-rows}` order). **✅ RESOLVED 2026-07-13 via ADR-0028 (serialize at tx-open):** `AmbientTransaction.EnsureStartedAsync` takes a **transaction-scoped exclusive `sp_getapplock`** ('acmp-audit-chain') immediately after `BeginTransaction` — before any module write — so every audited write-command acquires the chain lock first (one consistent order → no cross-handler deadlock) and appends serialize (no fork, no 1205). Held to commit ⇒ next command reads a committed tip; `THROW` on lock-timeout ⇒ fail-closed; SQL-Server-only (degrades to no-op elsewhere). The **denial/autocommit path** (no ambient tx) keeps the bounded retry as its backstop (broadened to catch the `PreviousHash` **or** `Hash` index race; deadlock-free — no crosswise module locks). Tests: `Concurrent_commands_all_commit_without_forking_the_audit_chain` (8 write-commands serialize) + `Concurrent_denials_all_record_their_audit_via_the_retry_without_forking_the_chain` (8 denials converge via retry) + the same-tx atomicity suite, all green (CI-proven for the write-command deadlock case). No schema/migration.

title: ADR-0038 DEPLOY PLUMBING (§5) — DONE 2026-08-12 (PR #237, main 122f41d). What shipped, and how it differs from the plan this row was raised with: THE CLIENT IS DEFINED IN reconcile.sh, NOT IN realm-export.json (DEF-049). Keycloak imports the bundled export only on FIRST run, so a client declared there reaches a fresh stack and never appears on prod or UAT — the DEF-023 / CHANGE-004 seam a third time. The client SECRET settled it: a secret can only be made to match gen-secrets' file by being SET from that file, so the client cannot be expressed in the export at all. reconcile.sh now creates-or-updates the client, re-asserts confidential + service-account-only on every run, sets the secret FROM the mounted file, and RECONCILES THE GRANT AS AN EXACT SET — revoking anything outside it, so a widened grant cannot survive a deploy — then reads the result back rather than trusting exit codes. THE GRANT IS `manage-users` AND NOTHING ELSE (OQ-070), and it now has a gate: check-realm-export.mjs asserts the EXACT set with realm-admin named forbidden, and BOTH failure branches were proven by forcing them (adding view-realm; granting realm-admin). The grant lives in deploy/keycloak/admin-client.env so the gate and the reconciler read the SAME value — a check reading a different file passes while the deployment drifts — and it needed a .gitignore exception, because `*.env` would have silently excluded the one file both of them depend on (the gate passed locally only because the file existed on disk). ENABLING IS ONE VARIABLE, which removes the boot-stopping sequencing hazard this row was raised warning about: the secret is ALWAYS written, unlike the Webex block, because a compose secrets: entry whose file is missing fails the whole stack, and because ValidateOnStart means a flag arriving before its secret STOPS api and worker rather than degrading. 09-put-env.sh now refuses that exact combination at the last point before it reaches a machine; gen-secrets GENERATES a value when unset rather than failing, so an operator .env predating the variable still boots — with no literal fallback, because a default credential in a script is a credential. The worker got identical config: it composes the same Membership module, so a flag without a secret would fail ITS validator too. VERIFIED SAFE FOR THE LIVE BOX BEFORE MERGING: 08-bootstrap-box.sh:164 runs gen-secrets BEFORE compose up at :207, so the new secret file always exists on a real deploy. ⚠ WHAT IS NOT YET EVIDENCED, AND THE DISTINCTION MATTERS: that the reconciler actually CREATED the client anywhere. CI's e2e boots the full stack against a real Keycloak and passed, but DEF-051 records that nothing depends on keycloak-config — so a failed reconcile leaves the stack healthy, and A GREEN E2E IS NOT EVIDENCE THE CLIENT EXISTS. Closing that assertion is DEF-051's job; the AC-090 behavioural leg additionally needs a deploy with KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ENABLED=true.

title: GUEST ACCESS WINDOWS FOLLOW THE MEETING - DONE 2026-08-12 (PR #244, main 5afe40f), and the row's own premise turned out to be FALSE. As raised this row said 'rescheduling a meeting does not move a guest's already-written window'. ACMP HAS NO RESCHEDULE: Meeting.ScheduledStart/End are private-set and assigned only in the Schedule factory, there is no PUT/PATCH on /api/meetings, and no feature mutates them - three independent checks. A meeting is scheduled once, then started, held or cancelled. So nothing was built for reschedule; IGuestWindowWriter takes an arbitrary instant precisely so a future reschedule can call it with the new end plus GuestAccess.Grace. WHAT DID SHIP is what DEC-041 added when it widened the scope, and those are the EXPOSURE cases rather than the inconvenience one: cancelling a meeting CLOSES its guest presenters' windows (an outsider must not keep live read access to material for a meeting that will not happen); removing the agenda item CLOSES it (the slot the access was granted for is gone); reassigning the slot CLOSES the replaced guest's window, while re-assigning the SAME person is a no-op. DESIGN NOTE WORTH KEEPING: IGuestWindowWriter is a SEPARATE port from IGuestProvisioner for availability, not tidiness - the provisioner is registered only when the Keycloak admin client is configured, so folding this in would have made CANCELLING A MEETING FAIL wherever in-app user management is off, which is every environment today. This port creates nothing (one nullable column) so it is registered unconditionally, like IPrincipalRevalidator. TWO SAFETY PROPERTIES, both proven by tests rather than argued: a guest holding a SECOND slot keeps their access (the rule is 'close it only if they no longer present any slot on a live meeting', checked against the store after the change, not reasoned about); and an ORDINARY member never acquires an expiry, because the port only touches rows that already hold a window - a member handed one by accident would be locked out of the whole product and DEF-029 means the row could never be deleted to recover.
activation_trigger: Reschedule: if a reschedule feature is ever built, it must call IGuestWindowWriter with the new ScheduledEnd + GuestAccess.Grace. Nothing else outstanding.

title: Stream.IsWildcard SHIPS WITH NO PRODUCTION READER, DELIBERATELY - and that is DW-026's exact signature, so it is registered here rather than left to be re-discovered as a fifth instance. WHAT LANDED (ADR-0042 step 1, PR 'feat/def-057-step1-seed-streams'): a bool column on membership.streams, a filtered unique index enforcing at most one wildcard row, and a seed of the committee's five delivery streams plus the wildcard. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST YET: any code that READS the column. Grep IsWildcard after this PR and you get the entity property, the EF configuration, the migration and the integration tests - and no production consumer. That is precisely how Topic.Reopen, Stream.Create, StreamScopeRequirement and Topic.SetScope each presented, so a reviewer applying DW-026's own lesson SHOULD flag this. This row is the answer to that flag. WHY IT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT, and the reasoning is ADR-0042's ordering, which the ADR calls load-bearing and non-negotiable: the reader is the authorization path, and wiring the authorization path before every member has been assigned a stream locks the entire committee out (all 26 production members were seeded straight into Keycloak, so the invite-time stream field does not cover them - ADR-0042 consequence (1), the one marked CERTAIN). The column must therefore EXIST, and be seeded, several PRs before anything consults it. Landing them together is the failure mode the ADR explicitly warns about: 'anyone treating it as one change will land the seed without the parts that make it safe'. THE NAMED FUTURE READER, so this is not an open-ended promise: UserStreamProvider (Membership.Infrastructure/Authorization/MembershipAbacProviders.cs), consumed by StreamScopeHandler, at ADR-0042 STEP 7. ⚠ THE READER CANNOT BE ADDED WITHOUT A PORT CHANGE, which is the real reason it is not a one-line follow-up: IUserStreamProvider.GetAssignedStreamsAsync returns IReadOnlyCollection<string> - a bare list of stream CODES. Wildcard-ness cannot travel through that return type without matching on the wildcard's code, which is EXACTLY what ADR-0042 clause (3) forbids (a magic string in an authorization control breaks silently on rename or re-code, or hands universal access to a future stream that collides with it). So step 7 must widen the port to carry the assigned codes AND a HasWildcard flag - symmetric with the AffectsAllStreams primitive bool that ADR-0042 clause (6) already mandates on IStreamScopedResource for the same cross-module reason (ADR-0001: the contract lives in Acmp.Shared.Contracts, the enum in Topics.Domain; ADR-0021 is the pattern). ⚠ UNTIL STEP 7 LANDS, ASSIGNING THE WILDCARD STREAM TO A MEMBER GRANTS NOTHING AND REFUSES NOTHING - it is inert data. It is not a latent bypass: no code path consults it, so it cannot widen access. The genuine risk in the interval is the opposite one - an administrator assigning 'All streams' through the (still to be built) UI and reasonably believing it took effect. That is why the assignment UI is step 3 and the wiring is step 7, with the backfill at step 5 in between. INVARIANT AT STAKE: same as DW-026 - a control that is never evaluated is indistinguishable from an implemented one. ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-15 (DEC-048 d1): THE TRIGGER FIRED AND THE PREMISE IS NO LONGER TRUE. The column now has THREE production readers - UserStreamProvider reads it and returns IsUnrestricted from ONE query (a flag from a column, never a code match, exactly as ADR-0042 clause (3) required), StreamScopeRequirement consumes that verdict, and the DEC-046 reconciliation grants that stream to every member row it creates. The port widening this row predicted as the blocker is what step 7 actually did. ⚠ What is NOT claimed by closing this: the wildcard path has not yet run in PRODUCTION - that is DEF-065's deploy step and is tracked there, not here.

SECOND, the claim is not right as written: FR-117 says 'viewable AND diffable', so 'viewable satisfies FR-117' satisfies half of it. THIRD, it defers to P14, which DEC-028 deferred INDEFINITELY - so the comment quietly converts a deferral-with-a-trigger into an abandonment. title: FR-037's DRAG-TO-REPRIORITIZE IS NOT BUILT: priority reordering is KEYBOARD-ONLY, and the drag that does exist changes STATUS, not priority. FR-037 reads 'As a Secretary or Chairman, I want to drag-and-drop topics to reprioritize them in the backlog, with priority stored as an explicit ordinal field, so that the committee's session order is always explicit.' THE ORDINAL HALF IS FULLY BUILT AND WELL TESTED: MoveTopicPriority materialises the column, orders it deterministically by (Priority, CreatedAt, Key), swaps the neighbour and renumbers 1..N contiguously, gated by BacklogPrioritize and audited - covered by Move_down_swaps_the_neighbour_and_renumbers_the_column_contiguously, Move_up_at_the_top_of_the_column_is_a_no_op, Move_is_denied_without_BacklogPrioritize, Move_rejects_a_decided_topic and Prioritize_sets_the_ordinal_and_audits. THE DRAG HALF IS NOT. In Kanban.tsx the only reorder path is onReorder, a keyboard +/-1 delta whose own comment attributes it to 'AC-043 / FR-034: keyboard reorder within a column'. The drag-and-drop that IS wired is column-level: the single onDrop sits on the section and calls requestMove(dragId, col.bucket), which changes the topic's STATUS - that is FR-033, a different requirement. No card-level drop handler exists, so dragging a card onto another card inside the same column does nothing. WHY THIS IS LOW AND NOT A DEFECT: the capability FR-037 exists to guarantee - an explicit, stored, auditable session order - IS delivered; only the input gesture differs, and the keyboard path is arguably the more accessible one. But the requirement names the gesture, so the divergence is real and was recorded nowhere.

title: NFR-030 CLAIMS FULL WCAG 2.2 AA CONFORMANCE AND ONLY THE MACHINE-CHECKABLE SUBSET IS VERIFIED. NFR-030 (priority Must) reads 'All user interface components shall conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA' with the target '100% of applicable success criteria'. WHAT IS BUILT IS GENUINELY STRONG: axe-core runs across roughly 40 component suites plus a dedicated a11y.test.tsx covering the login page, the shell chrome, the side navigation, the admin surfaces and the backlog table, and every one is asserted axe-clean. THE GAP IS THAT AUTOMATED SCANNING CANNOT ESTABLISH THE CLAIM. axe-core detects only a portion of WCAG success criteria by construction - it cannot judge whether alternative text is MEANINGFUL rather than merely present, whether focus order is LOGICAL rather than merely defined, whether an error message is ACTIONABLE, or whether a reading sequence makes sense in Arabic RTL. Those need a human pass with a screen reader and keyboard. ⚠ WHY NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION WAS WRITTEN FOR NFR-030: an AC recording Partial would hold package readiness false permanently, because acs-met counts by retired_in and requires the LATEST verdict to be Met (trap 16c). So the honest instrument for a requirement that is genuinely part-verified is a deferred-work row with a trigger, not an AC carrying a verdict that can never go green until the manual work happens. SIZING: a keyboard-and-screen-reader pass over the primary flows in both EN and RTL, against the WCAG 2.2 AA checklist, recording what it finds - a day or two of focused work, not a project.
activation_trigger: Before any external accessibility assertion is made - a procurement questionnaire, a VPAT, an accessibility statement on the product, or a compliance review that asks for WCAG 2.2 AA conformance. Also fires if a user with assistive technology reports a barrier, since that is evidence the automated subset was not enough. Until one of those, the axe-clean gate across 40 surfaces is a strong and honest partial control and the gap is recorded rather than hidden.

title: NFR-035's 'NO HARDCODED DISPLAY STRINGS' CLAUSE HAS NO CONTROL, while its other clause is well guarded. NFR-035 reads 'All UI strings shall be externalized in react-i18next resource files; no hardcoded display strings in components.' THE EXTERNALIZATION HALF IS GUARDED: scripts/check-i18n.mjs gates CI on EN/AR key parity (1901 keys, reported green this session) and additionally catches mojibake, where Arabic values were written as Latin-1-decoded UTF-8 - a real defect class this project has hit before. THE 'NO HARDCODED STRINGS' HALF IS NOT GUARDED AT ALL. check-i18n compares the two resource files against each other; it cannot see a component. Nothing else fills the gap: .oxlintrc.json carries no rule against literal JSX text, and there is no equivalent check anywhere in scripts/ or the workflows. So a developer who types a label directly into a component ships an untranslatable string that the i18n gate is structurally incapable of noticing - the EN/AR files stay in perfect parity because the string never entered them. SIZING: an oxlint or eslint rule flagging bare text nodes in JSX, or a targeted script scanning components for string literals in render position, with an allowlist for the genuinely non-display cases (test ids, aria roles, class names). Small, but it needs an allowlist to be usable at all, which is the part that takes the time.
activation_trigger: When a hardcoded display string actually reaches the UI and is noticed - most likely as an English word appearing in the Arabic interface, which is how this class of bug always surfaces. Also worth activating alongside any future i18n work that touches many components at once, since that is when the rule is cheapest to introduce and most likely to catch existing strays.

title: NFR-011 (single file <= 100 MB; no application cap on total storage) IS MOSTLY CHECKABLE AND WAS NOT SEPARATED OUT, which this row records honestly. The per-file ceiling is a CONFIGURED VALUE - MeetingRecordingOptions and the topic attachment options carry it, and MeetingRecordingApiTests already forces the oversize refusal - so a criterion over the validators would verify most of it. What cannot be verified from the repository is that a 100 MB upload actually SUCCEEDS end to end through nginx, Kestrel and MinIO, which is where request-size limits usually bite, and the 'no application-level cap on total storage' clause is a negative about code that would need a stated instrument.

Activate when someone actually needs the 100 MB ceiling confirmed end to end - a large recording upload failing is the realistic trigger.

title: NFR-012 (audit log sustains >= 100 append-only writes/second for 60 s without data loss or lock contention) IS NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THIS REPOSITORY, and it is the performance row most worth eventually measuring. The audit chain is HASH-LINKED, so every append depends on the previous row's hash - a design that is correct and inherently serialising, and exactly the shape where sustained throughput can surprise you. AuditAtomicityTests already proves concurrent commands do not FORK the chain, which is the correctness question; the throughput question is separate and unmeasured. SIZING: a sustained-write harness against the real SQL Server container, measuring inserts/second and lock waits over 60 s.
activation_trigger: Before any change to how audit rows are written - batching, an outbox, or moving the hash chain - since those are the changes that would break sustained throughput. Also if audit writes are ever implicated in a lock-contention incident.

title: NFR-013 (columnstore-indexed dashboard aggregations <= 3 000 ms P95 over ~50 000 rows) IS NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THIS REPOSITORY, and it carries a second question worth separating: the requirement asserts a columnstore index as the mechanism, and whether one exists is a SCHEMA fact checkable today, independent of any timing. The dashboard is also composed CLIENT-SIDE over several existing registers rather than by a single aggregation query, so what to time is itself a design question the measurement would have to settle first.

title: NFR-063's 'NOT OPTIMIZED FOR MOBILE' NOTICE DOES NOT EXIST. NFR-063 reads: mobile phone viewports (< 768 px) need not be supported in v1, and 'a "not optimized for mobile" notice is acceptable on narrow viewports', with the target 'Mobile (< 768 px) displays a graceful not-optimized notice; no broken layout'. THE NO-BROKEN-LAYOUT HALF IS PLAUSIBLY MET: real breakpoints exist at 900, 860, 760, 720 and 560 px across 27 stylesheets, so the layout stacks rather than shattering. THE NOTICE DOES NOT EXIST. A scan of en.json - 2219 key-value pairs, so the instrument demonstrably had a subject - finds no 'not optimi', 'mobile', 'small screen' or 'desktop' string anywhere, and no component renders such a banner. title: NFR-037 IS BUILT ON ITS DATE SIDE AND ESSENTIALLY UNBUILT ON ITS NUMBER SIDE, WHICH IS WHY IT GETS THIS ROW RATHER THAN AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION. NFR-037 (Must, Approved) reads: 'All date, time, and number formats shall use locale-appropriate formatting: Gregorian calendar in both EN and AR (v1 only; Hijri display is a future option, not in v1). Target: Gregorian dates rendered correctly in both locales; no raw ISO strings visible.' THE DATE AND TIME HALF HOLDS AND WAS MEASURED. A census of every date-formatting call site in the SPA finds 31 uses of Intl.DateTimeFormat and ZERO uses of toLocaleDateString or toLocaleString anywhere outside tests. Of those 31, 29 pass the live UI language (i18n.language or a lang prop) and the remaining two are deliberate and documented: p15Date.formatDmy pins ar-u-nu-arab so Arabic-Indic digits render identically under Node and browser ICU, and auditMeta.formatTimestamp fixes the TIME portion to en-GB with numberingSystem latn and hour12 false so an audit trail reads as a 24-hour Latin-digit clock in both locales while its DATE portion still switches on language. No calendar option anywhere selects anything but gregory, which agrees with DEC-015, CON-012 and INV-009. A scan of the 184 SPA source files for date-shaped values interpolated into JSX without a formatter returns nine candidates and all nine are false positives - three are i18n keys and six are local fmt or fmtDate helpers that wrap Intl - so no bare ISO string was found on the surfaces that scan can see. The entire SPA contains exactly TWO Intl.NumberFormat call sites: WikiReadingView's fmtCount, which correctly switches to ar-u-nu-arab, and SessionPage's byte-size formatter. Everything else a user reads as a number - vote tallies, backlog counts, time-box minutes, percentages, list totals, attachment sizes outside that one path - is rendered bare, so it appears in Latin digits regardless of locale while the dates beside it render in Arabic-Indic. This is not a rounding error against the requirement's text; it is one of three named format families being unimplemented. This is the settled rule. DO NOT LET A LATER SESSION HELPFULLY ADD THE MISSING CRITERION - the gap is real work. title: NFR-039'S 'SINGLE SOURCE OF CANONICAL BILINGUAL TERMS' DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE TWO DOCUMENTS THAT CLAIM TO BE IT POINT AT EACH OTHER. NFR-039 (Must, Approved) reads: 'The EN-AR terminology glossary (README section G, localized in design handoff) shall be the single source of canonical bilingual terms; no term shall have more than one AR translation within the application. Target: 0 terminology inconsistencies detected in the i18n resource files.' CLAUSE ONE IS UNMET AND THIS IS PROVABLE WITHOUT READING ANY ARABIC. README.md section G (line 167) is a single paragraph listing 22 English committee terms and its own heading says 'EN-AR pairing finalized in design handoff'. It contains ZERO Arabic characters - measured, with a control proving the detector works, since the same pattern finds 1889 Arabic lines in ar.json. The design handoff (design-handoff/claude-design-input-package.md line 113) says: 'Consistent EN-AR terminology (a shared glossary - see /docs/README section G)'. SO EACH DOCUMENT NAMES THE OTHER AS THE SOURCE AND NEITHER CONTAINS A SINGLE ARABIC TERM. The third candidate, DOC-049 at docs/governance/glossary.md, is EN-only too and states outright in its own preamble that 'EN-AR term pairing is maintained in the design and i18n resources, not in this file' - and it lives under docs/, the frozen read-only archive superseded 2026-07-22. The canonical Arabic that DOES exist is scattered: DEC-032 (Approved) fixes the term family for 'Architecture' as الهيكلة, and everything else lives only in ar.json, which is the artifact the requirement wants CHECKED AGAINST the glossary and therefore cannot also be the glossary. CLAUSE TWO WAS MEASURED AND IS NOT ADJUDICABLE BY A READER OF CODE, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT THING FROM UNMEASURED. Pairing all 1901 keys and grouping short labels of four words or fewer gives 1037 distinct English labels, of which 76 carry more than one Arabic rendering. THAT 76 IS NOT A DEFECT COUNT AND MUST NOT BE REPORTED AS ONE. Arabic adjectives agree in gender with the noun they describe, so 'Accepted' is مقبول describing a risk and مقبولة describing a recommendation, and BOTH ARE CORRECT - collapsing them would be the bug, not the fix. DEC-032 makes the same point about definiteness, recording that dropping ال inside a genitive construct is a grammar RULE rather than a string substitution. Classifying the 76 by whether the renderings share an Arabic stem: 55 are morphological (gender, definiteness, plural) and presumed correct, and 21 are lexically distinct - one concept rendered with genuinely different words. EVEN THE 21 IS A CANDIDATE SET RATHER THAN A FINDING SET, and the instrument's own limits say why: 'Open' splits into مفتوح and فتح, which is an adjective and a verb doing different jobs correctly, and 'Minutes' splits into محضر and المحاضر, which is a BROKEN PLURAL that crude suffix-stripping cannot relate to its singular. THE SINGLE STRONGEST CANDIDATE, offered for an Arabic reader to judge and deliberately NOT filed as a defect: 'Urgency' renders as الإلحاح on the research surface and as الأهمية on the topics surface, and الأهمية means importance rather than urgency - so this may be a mistranslation rather than an inconsistency. THE TARGET CLAUSE HAS NO DETECTING INSTRUMENT AT ALL, which is the finding that outlives the rest. title: NFR-033 IS VERIFIED ON ONE OF ITS TWO THRESHOLDS AND ON NONE OF THE FOUR STATES IT NAMES. NFR-033 (Must, Approved) requires colour contrast for all text on background AND FOR UI COMPONENT STATES - normal, hover, focused, disabled - to meet WCAG 2.2 AA, and states two thresholds explicitly: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI components. WHAT EXISTS IS BETTER THAN MOST GATES IN THIS REPOSITORY AND SHOULD NOT BE UNDERSOLD. src/Acmp.Web/src/styles/contrast.test.ts parses tokens.css directly, computes real WCAG relative luminance and contrast ratios, and asserts 20 foreground-on-background token pairs in BOTH the light and the explicit dark palettes - plus a third assertion that the OS-default dark palette inside the prefers-color-scheme media query is IDENTICAL to the explicit one, because they are two hand-maintained copies and only one was reachable by the checks. It also carries its own anti-vacuity guard: before comparing the two dark palettes it asserts the parsed block contains more than ten tokens, so a selector that stopped matching cannot pass by comparing nothing to nothing. THAT GUARD EXISTS BECAUSE THE TEST WAS ONCE FALSELY GREEN in exactly that way - its header records that a plain indexOf matched the selector inside a PROSE COMMENT and returned the LIGHT palette for every dark case, for the file's entire life until 2026-08-10. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, AND IT IS HALF THE REQUIREMENT. Every one of the 20 pairs is asserted at 4.5:1. NOT ONE uses the 3:1 threshold, so the requirement's 'large text and UI components' clause has no case at all - no border-on-background pair, no focus-ring pair, no disabled-state pair. And the four states the requirement names by name - normal, hover, focused, disabled - are absent from the pair table entirely; tokens.css contains only six focus, hover or disabled mentions in total. SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN THE REQUIREMENT TOO: the file's own header says it covers 'the design tokens the Topics screens rely on', not the application. AND THE RENDERED QUESTION IS UNTOUCHED BY DESIGN: color-contrast is explicitly disabled in BOTH axe passes, the jsdom one because there is no layout engine and the live Playwright one by convention, so nothing anywhere measures contrast as actually painted - only as declared in tokens.

title: NFR-023'S ABSOLUTE-SESSION CEILING IS SATISFIED BY A KEYCLOAK DEFAULT THAT ACMP NEVER CHOSE AND DOES NOT PIN. AC-139 records NFR-023 Met, and the idle half of that verdict is solid - thirty-minute app-side inactivity detection, built deliberately under OQ-076, mutation-tested, 100 percent covered. THE ABSOLUTE HALF IS DIFFERENT IN KIND AND THIS ROW EXISTS TO SAY SO. The clause is that refresh tokens shall not extend a session beyond twenty-four hours without re-authentication, and what satisfies it is ssoSessionMaxLifespan, measured at 36000 seconds - ten hours - on the LIVE PRODUCTION realm via kcadm on 2026-08-13. Ten hours is comfortably inside twenty-four. But deploy/keycloak/realm-export.json sets NEITHER ssoSessionIdleTimeout NOR ssoSessionMaxLifespan: a grep for either key across every json and shell file in the repository returns nothing. So the value is not ACMP's decision at all - it is whatever the Keycloak image defaults to, observed once, eight days before this row was written. NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY WOULD FAIL IF IT CHANGED. A Keycloak image bump could raise the maximum lifespan past twenty-four hours and every test, every gate and every acceptance criterion would stay green, because none of them reads it. This is the same shape as NFR-050: a property that is TRUE across everything measured, and GUARDED by nothing - except that NFR-050's property is a fact about migrations already written, while this one is a fact about a third party's default that can change under a version bump. TWO FURTHER THINGS WORTH KEEPING TOGETHER HERE, because they are the same configuration surface. First, realm-export.json reaches FRESH stacks only, which this project has already been bitten by - so pinning the values there fixes new environments and does nothing for the running ones, and reconcile.sh is the only seam to those. Second, OQ-003's resolution names a 60-minute idle timeout while the realm and the application both implement 30; that inconsistency is recorded inside OQ-076 and is harmless against NFR-023's ceilings, but anyone pinning these values should settle which number is intended rather than pinning whichever one they happen to read first.
activation_trigger: Whenever the Keycloak image is next bumped - that is the exact moment an unpinned default can change underneath the requirement, and it is also when someone is already editing the realm configuration. Also fires if a fresh environment is ever stood up, since a fresh stack inherits the image default rather than an ACMP decision, and immediately if anyone proposes changing the app-side idle timeout, because the two halves need to stay coherent. CHEAPEST FIRST STEP: add ssoSessionIdleTimeout and ssoSessionMaxLifespan to realm-export.json with the values that were measured, so a fresh stack gets ACMP's numbers rather than the image's. That alone converts an inherited default into a stated decision. The reconcile path is the separate half - realm-export.json reaches FRESH stacks only, so an existing environment needs reconcile.sh to carry the same values or the two drift.

title: NFR-019 IS KEPT AS THE TARGET AND TWO OF ITS THREE HOPS RUN PLAINTEXT: THIS IS THAT GAP, TRACKED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED. Operator disposition DEC-066, 2026-08-20: NFR-019 stays as written and this row carries the divergence. WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNENCRYPTED, measured. deploy/nginx/cloud-443.conf.template proxies to http://keycloak:8080/ at line 121 and to http://api:8080 at line 145; deploy/nginx/default.conf.template does the same for dev at line 58; and KeycloakAdmin__BaseUrl defaults to http://keycloak:8080/ in BOTH compose files. So everything behind the reverse proxy speaks unencrypted HTTP over the Docker network. WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, and should not be re-done by whoever takes this: the PUBLIC edge is configured exactly to the floor NFR-019 states - cloud-443.conf.template line 30 sets ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3, with certificates published by certbot-deploy-hook.sh - and the application-to-SQL-Server hop is encrypted, the connection string carrying Encrypt=True. The Tarseem hop the requirement names has no endpoint at all: P14 was deferred indefinitely by DEC-028 and a repository-wide search for the name returns one hit, a placeholder page. So the work is the Keycloak and api hops, not all three. TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS LARGER THAN A CONFIG EDIT. First, service-to-service TLS needs a certificate story - who issues, who rotates, and what each container trusts - and the existing certbot flow does not extend to it, because those certificates are for a public hostname while these services address each other by compose service name. Second, the VERSION FLOOR is unpinned everywhere except the public edge: no SslProtocols setting, no MinProtocol, no ssl_protocols directive exists on any internal hop, so even after TLS is introduced the 'TLS 1.0 and 1.1 shall be disabled' clause would still rest on image defaults - the same shape as DW-073, where NFR-023's absolute ceiling is satisfied by a Keycloak default nobody chose. WHY THIS IS A DEFERRED-WORK ROW AND NFR-019 HAS NO ACCEPTANCE CRITERION: the requirement cannot record Met while two of the hops it names are plaintext, and an AC recording Partial would hold package readiness false permanently because acs-met counts by retired_in and ignores lifecycle_status. NFR-019 sits exactly where NFR-054 sits behind DW-066 - deliberately unverifiable, with the register stating the target rather than the status quo. DO NOT LET A LATER SESSION ADD THE MISSING CRITERION.

Also fires if an external security review or the NFR-018 ASVS assessment examines transport security, since this is exactly what such a review looks for; and whenever nginx or Keycloak is next reconfigured, because that is when the certificate plumbing is already open. ⚠ DO NOT START THIS AS A SIDE EFFECT OF SOMETHING ELSE: it needs a certificate story for service-to-service trust (who issues, who rotates, what the containers trust) and that is a design decision, not a config edit. title: ToastProvider IS BUILT, TESTED AND MOUNTED NOWHERE - the app has a transient-feedback mechanism no feature can use. Found 2026-08-21 while building WBS-23.3's PNG export, which needed exactly this and could not have it. `src/components/ui/Toast.tsx` exports a full `ToastProvider` (portalled `aria-live="polite"` region, queue, 5s auto-dismiss, three tones, dismiss button) and a `useToast()` hook that THROWS 'useToast must be used within a ToastProvider' when no provider is above it. A repository-wide search for `ToastProvider` and `useToast` outside the component's own file returns exactly one file: `overlays.test.tsx`, its own test. So the provider is never mounted in the application tree, `useToast()` would throw from any real screen, and the component's own doc comment cites Design System section 12 for a mechanism the product cannot reach. It arrived in the big design-fidelity import (`16f2f8b`, PR #9) alongside the rest of the shared component library and nothing has wired it since. THIS IS THE 'already half-built' SHAPE the project keeps meeting, and it is worth stating precisely: the component is NOT dead code in the usual sense - it is correct, covered and ready - it is simply unreachable, and a green test suite over a component nobody mounts says nothing about whether the app has toasts. WHAT WBS-23.3 DID INSTEAD, so this row is not read as a defect against that build: PNG-export failure feedback is rendered inline in the card as a `.rpt-card-note` with `role="status"`, reusing a class that already exists. That is the right call for one button - mounting an app-wide provider to give one feature a failure message would be a far larger change than the feature - but it is the SECOND ad-hoc transient-feedback treatment in this codebase and a third will make the inconsistency the real cost. NOT SIZED AS TRIVIAL, because the interesting part is not the mount. Wiring `ToastProvider` into the app shell is a few lines; deciding WHICH existing ad-hoc confirmations and failure notices should become toasts, and localising `regionLabel` (it currently defaults to the untranslated English string 'Notifications'), is the actual work, and it touches screens across several modules.
activation_trigger: EITHER of two events, and the first is the more likely: (a) a third feature needs transient success/failure feedback and is about to invent a third ad-hoc treatment - at that point the inconsistency is established and wiring the provider is cheaper than the third bespoke one; or (b) a design-fidelity or accessibility pass takes up Design System section 12, which the component's own header cites. NOT triggered by the component merely existing unmounted - it costs nothing where it sits, breaks nothing, and this row exists so that fact is recorded rather than rediscovered. ⚠ Whoever activates it must localise `regionLabel`, which today defaults to a hardcoded English 'Notifications' and would ship an untranslated accessible name into an aria-live region the moment the provider is mounted.

title:
TopicSource IS A NINE-VALUE DOMAIN VOCABULARY THAT NO SURFACE IN THE PRODUCT HAS EVER SHOWN OR OFFERED, AND IT HAS NO BILINGUAL LABELS AT ALL. Found 2026-08-21 while building WBS-23.4, which needed to decide whether the reclassify dialog should offer a source picker beside the type picker. THE FACTS, checked rather than assumed: `TopicSource` declares nine values (CommitteeMember, StreamRequest, UrgentOrgNeed, OperationalIncident, SecurityFinding, Modernization, InnovationInitiative, CrossStreamProblem, Regulatory). `SubmitTopic.tsx` sends a hardcoded `SOURCE_DEFAULT` and its own header records that as a P5a decision - the submitter never chooses one. A search of both locale bundles for any of the nine names returns ZERO keys; the only hit anywhere is `audit.entity.CommitteeMember`, which is a different vocabulary that happens to share a word. So every topic in the product carries a source, the domain and the API both take it, and no human has ever seen or set one.

WHY WBS-23.4 DID NOT ADD THE PICKER, so this is not read as an oversight. Exposing source means authoring EIGHTEEN new strings - nine English and nine Arabic - for governance concepts, and the Arabic half is the problem: NFR-039 requires a single canonical source of bilingual terms, LL-010 records that the glossary it names is a circular pointer between two English documents and does not exist, and DW-069 carries building it. Inventing nine Arabic governance terms inside a feature slice is exactly what that requirement forbids, and it would seed terminology the glossary would later have to either bless or contradict. The reclassify endpoint therefore takes BOTH fields, because the domain method does and the API is the contract; the SPA sends the topic's existing source back unchanged.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BLOCKED AND WHAT IS NOT. The API is NOT blocked - a caller can already correct a source today through POST /api/topics/{id}/reclassify, and AC-143 says so while deliberately not claiming a UI for it. What is blocked is the UI, and only on the terminology.
activation_trigger: EITHER: (a) DW-069's bilingual glossary exists and can supply the nine Arabic terms, at which point this is a small picker beside the type one and the strings are a transcription rather than an invention; or (b) a Secretary reports that a topic's source is wrong and cannot be corrected in-product - the same demand-shaped trigger DW-032 carried, and the operator is the demand channel it names. ⚠ NOT triggered by the field merely being invisible: it has been invisible since v1, nothing depends on it being visible, and the endpoint already accepts corrections. ⚠ Whoever activates it must ALSO decide whether source becomes visible on read surfaces (topic detail, backlog facets), because a field a user can set but not see afterwards is worse than one they can do neither with.

title:
EVERY DIALOG THAT PAIRS A DESCRIPTION WITH A FORM FIELD RENDERS THE FIRST FIELD LABEL FLUSH AGAINST THE DESCRIPTION - a shared design-system spacing gap, NOT a defect in any one screen. `Dialog.tsx` renders the description and then `{children}` with nothing between them; `.dialog-desc` carries `margin: 0`, and `.field` only gets top spacing from `.field + .field`, which by definition cannot apply to the FIRST field. So the first label always sits directly under the description's last line.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and this is the part worth copying. WBS-23.4's new reclassify dialog looked cramped in a browser check - the kind of thing JSDOM cannot see. Rather than fix it locally or change shared CSS on a hunch, the SHIPPED convert dialog was rendered in the same harness as a CONTROL, and it has the identical spacing. That settled it by evidence: the new dialog MATCHES the application rather than introducing anything, so changing it alone would have made it the inconsistent one.

SIZING, measured rather than guessed. The fix is one rule - roughly `.dialog-desc + .field { margin-block-start: var(--sp-4) }` in `overlays.css`. The COST is not the rule, it is the verification: `<Field>` renders `.field`, so around twenty dialogs across actions, decisions, dependencies, governance, meetings, research, risks, administration and topics would all shift, and a design-system spacing change wants each of them looked at rather than a green suite. HOW THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS SURVIVED, which is the more useful half: I had TWO execution paths failing identically, Testcontainers and plain docker-compose, and read that as independent corroboration. THEY WERE NOT INDEPENDENT - both build deploy/Dockerfile.sqlserver, so only the orchestration differed while the thing under test was identical. BUILD THE OWASP ASVS 5.0 LEVEL 2 EVIDENCE PACK FOR NFR-018 - AN INPUT TO AN ASSESSMENT, NOT THE ASSESSMENT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE ROW. NFR-018 (Must, Approved) requires the application to meet OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2 for all applicable chapters. It is the ONLY remaining requirement that real work could close, and it cannot be closed from inside this repository: Level 2 conformance is established by an external assessor, not by self-assertion. This row produces the document that maps the controls THIS CODEBASE ALREADY HAS to the L2 chapters, so an assessor does not start cold and does not bill for rediscovering what is already built.

WHY IT EXISTS AS AN OVERRIDE, recorded so nobody reads it as a settled judgement. The agent recommended leaving NFR-018 alone: it is blocked on a third party, no trigger had fired, and preparation without a consumer is speculative work. The operator chose 'Prepare the evidence pack now' (DEC-072 d4), on the view that an assessor starting cold is a cost paid later at worse rates.

WHAT THIS ROW MUST NOT BECOME, and a later session will be tempted. IT DOES NOT CLOSE NFR-018. The requirement stays Approved and correctly carries NO acceptance criterion, because acs-met counts by retired_in and ignores lifecycle_status, so an AC written ahead of an assessor's report would hold package readiness false forever (trap 16c). DO NOT write an acceptance criterion for NFR-018 out of this pack, and do not let the pack's own completeness be mistaken for conformance - a map of existing controls to chapters is a claim about coverage of the DOCUMENT, never about the adequacy of the controls, which is precisely the judgement an assessor is paid to make.

WHAT THE PACK SHOULD CARRY, and much of it already exists as evidence in this package. The authorization model and its per-request revalidation (ADR-0039, AC-090), the deny-by-default read gate (DEF-052's GuestSurfaceMiddleware), the hash-linked immutable audit chain, the confidentiality ABAC with egress redaction (SL-030, AV-192), secret handling, the session and idle-timeout behaviour (useIdleSignOut.ts), input validation as it is actually enforced - in the DOMAIN for the four commands carrying scalar input, which an endpoint-level census gets wrong (LL-006). IT MUST ALSO CARRY THE KNOWN GAPS HONESTLY, or it is worse than no pack: DEF-100 and DW-074 record that two of NFR-019's three internal hops run plaintext by design, and an assessor will look for exactly that. A pack that omits a gap the register already holds is the manufactured-status move DEF-010 records.
activation_trigger: ALREADY ACTIVATED by DEC-072 d4, 2026-08-23. Not blocked on anything external - the pack is built from what this repository already contains, and it is the half of NFR-018 that does not need an assessor. The row CLOSES when the pack exists and is reviewed; NFR-018 itself closes only when an external assessor's report exists to evidence it, which is a separate act the operator commissions. If an assessment IS later commissioned, re-scope the pack to that assessor's stated scope rather than shipping the speculative version - DW-074 and DEF-100 both name transport security as the thing such a review examines first.

Both pull requests were INVISIBLE when DEC-072 d1 authorised 'sweep everything, majors included', because the gh pr list behind that description carried --limit 10 and these two sat past position ten (PE-599). They are the OLDEST rows in the queue, 2026-07-16, and the listing is newest-first, so the cap truncated exactly the end where the largest and most-aged work lived. THE OPERATOR WAS RE-ASKED WITH THE CORRECTED FACTS RATHER THAN HAVING THE WORD 'EVERYTHING' STRETCHED OVER WORK THEY HAD NEVER SEEN.

Alpine is musl rather than glibc, and this application talks to SQL Server through Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and does culture-aware work in Arabic and English - globalization and native interop are exactly where musl breaks, and ICU behaviour differs. Distroless avoids musl but has no shell, which changes the healthcheck and any entrypoint that shells out. FULL e2e LEG, and verify Arabic search (FREETEXT, LCID 1025) END TO END before believing any of it. A .NET major on top of that means the migration and the base change can each mask the other, so land them in an order that lets you attribute a failure - runtime first on the existing Debian base, then the base move - rather than in one commit.

It cannot record Met while api and worker sit on a Debian base, and DW-066 is the only route to an acceptance criterion for that clause. GitHub forbids self-approval, so configuring required_approving_review_count=1 on main would block every merge this project makes, including its own author's. DEF-105's fix therefore set it to 0: pull requests are required and all nine status checks are required, but no human approval is, and that is the honest maximum for a single-operator repository.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE IN DEF-105: DEF-105's claim was that no branch protection existed, and that claim is now false, so the row is Fixed. This clause is a DIFFERENT and smaller divergence - a narrative document stating a rule that cannot be satisfied by the current team - and folding an unresolved residual into a Fixed row is how residuals get lost. ANSWERED BY EXPERIMENT: coverage-v8 v4 IS THE MORE HONEST COUNTER, NOT THE BROKEN ONE, AND THE ~20 'REGRESSED' FILES WERE NEVER COVERED IN THE FIRST PLACE. The question was whether v4's numbers are more correct than v3's or less, because PR #307 - which bumps vitest and @vitest/coverage-v8 to 4.1.11 together, necessary since each pins an exact peer on the other - passes EVERY TEST and fails only ADR-0016's per-file line gate, over about twenty files byte-identical to main.

THE EXPERIMENT, run exactly as this row's cheapest-first-step specified: same source, same test file, same three passing tests, coverage under v3 then under v4, on src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx - chosen because it is 55 lines and therefore hand-countable. Run in a container, because six orphaned vite dev servers hold a native binary open on the host and npm ci cannot complete there. RESULT: v3 reports 100% lines and no uncovered line. v4 reports 90% lines and names exactly ONE line - line 30.

LINE 30 IS: a Button whose onClick is an inline arrow calling window.location.reload(). The three tests render the fallback, so the JSX on that line genuinely executes; the third test clicks the OTHER button on line 31, the go-to-dashboard action. NOTHING EVER CLICKS RELOAD, so the arrow function body never runs. The line therefore PARTIALLY executed: element created, callback never invoked.

WHAT THE COVERAGE DATA SHOWS, and it is the decisive part because BOTH PROVIDERS AGREE ON THE FACTS. Each one's function map records the same uncalled function on line 30 - v3 names it onClick, v4 names it anonymous_1. They differ only in WHERE they count it. v3 records ZERO statements with zero hits, so its line map is clean and line 30 is credited. v4 records STATEMENT 3 with zero hits, and that propagates into the line metric. The disagreement is not about what executed; it is about whether an uninvoked callback makes its LINE uncovered.

WHY v4 IS THE RIGHT ANSWER FOR THIS GATE SPECIFICALLY. ADR-0016's threshold is LINES ONLY - the config comment says so in as many words, 'functions/branches are not the basis'. Under v3 that makes every untested inline handler INVISIBLE to the gate, because the line is credited for the JSX wrapped around the callback while the callback itself is only ever reflected in the functions percentage nobody gates on. v4 makes it count. THE UPGRADE DOES NOT LOWER COVERAGE; IT CLOSES A HOLE THAT MADE 'LINES ONLY' WEAKER THAN IT SOUNDS.

SCOPE OF THE CLAIM, stated honestly: this is PROVEN for ErrorBoundary.tsx and the mechanism - inline arrow handlers in JSX - is pervasive in React components, which is what all twenty of the affected files are. That makes the generalisation highly likely but not measured. EACH OTHER FILE SHOULD BE SPOT-CHECKED THE SAME WAY BEFORE ITS TESTS ARE WRITTEN, because a different file could be failing for a different reason and would then get the wrong fix.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: lowering the threshold to clear the red. That was already forbidden by this row and the experiment strengthens the ban - the number would be hiding a real gap rather than an artefact. Equally, REFUSING THE UPGRADE on the grounds that v4 miscounts is now unsupported.
activation_trigger: ANSWERED; WHAT REMAINS IS WORK AND ONE OPERATOR CHOICE. The work is writing the missing tests for the untested inline handlers that v4 exposes - roughly twenty files, each needing its uncovered lines identified the same way (run the file's test under v4 with coverage and read the named lines) and a test that actually invokes the handler. THE OPERATOR CHOOSES THE SHAPE: (a) write the missing tests first and merge #307 once the gate passes honestly, which is the only route that ends with both a current vitest and a true 95%; or (b) merge #307 with a deliberately recorded, time-boxed re-baseline naming every file and its number, so the gap is visible rather than averaged away; or (c) stay on vitest 3 and accept that the lines-only gate cannot see untested inline handlers - which should then be written into ADR-0016 rather than left implicit. ⚠ #307, #261 and #137 stay OPEN until this is chosen; #307 supersedes the other two in content and closing it would lose the paired bump.

title:
VISUAL-VERIFY HARNESSES LEAK AS PROCESSES AND NOTHING TEARS THEM DOWN - trap 28 GUARDS THE FILES AND MISSES THE PROCESSES, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY SIX SURVIVED THIRTEEN DAYS. Found 2026-08-23: six vite dev servers plus their six npx parents, all rooted in src/Acmp.Web/node_modules, on ports 5199, 5201, 5233, 5241, 4173 and 8124, started across 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-21 by earlier sessions' visual-verify work - two of them carrying a .vp argument, which is the tell. They held rolldown-binding.win32-x64-msvc.node open, so npm ci and npm install failed on the host with EPERM and EBUSY, and an npm ci that unlinks node_modules before reinstalling gutted the tree from 171 packages to 35 partway through. Killing exactly those twelve restored npm ci to a clean exit and 171 packages, verified by running it rather than assumed.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW RATHER THAN A ONE-OFF CLEANUP: trap 28 already says to delete throwaway visual-verify harnesses before committing, because vr-out/ is gitignored but a vr-*.tsx in src/ is not and would ship. THAT GUARD IS ABOUT FILES. The visual-verify loop also starts a long-lived dev server, and nothing anywhere stops it. A file-level check runs clean over a machine with six leaked servers on it, which is precisely what happened - the working tree was clean all along.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS, and this is the part that cost real time: the failure does not present as leaked processes. It presents as npm refusing to install with an opaque Windows EPERM on a native binary, in a session that has nothing to do with visual verification, days or weeks later. The diagnosis requires enumerating node processes and matching their command lines against the repo path, which nobody does by default. A leaked process is a booby trap with a long fuse and no label.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT: the loop that STARTS a visual-verify server should be the thing that stops it - a trap or finally that kills the pid it launched, or a fixed port plus a pre-flight kill of anything already on it, so a crashed session cannot leave one behind. A cleanup step that lives only in a checklist is the same shape as the branch-protection claim DEF-105 recorded: a control that exists in prose and not in machinery. ⚠ The check must also be able to FAIL LOUDLY: a sweep that finds no leaked servers and one that cannot see them look identical, which is trap 31.
activation_trigger: Whenever a visual-verify harness is next started - that is the moment the teardown belongs, and the cheapest fix is to make starting and stopping one operation rather than two. Also fires immediately if npm ci or npm install fails again on this machine with EPERM or EBUSY on a file under node_modules: enumerate node processes, match their command lines against the repo path, and read this row before debugging npm. ⚠ DO NOT treat that failure as an npm bug or a corrupted lockfile - it is a file lock held by a process from a previous session, and npm ci makes it WORSE by unlinking node_modules before it discovers it cannot finish.
